source: Vicente (1999) Cognitive Work Analysis (book; five phases as summarised on Wikipedia)
finding: CWA has five phases: work domain analysis, control task analysis, strategies analysis, social organisation and cooperation analysis, worker competencies analysis. Work domain analysis comes first and models the system itself, not the user.
numbers: 5 phases. Wikipedia page lists them but gives no study numbers.
limits: Secondary source only. The book itself was not opened.
agent_relevance: S0 gate: before any attempt, write down what the job is for, which constraints bind it, and what can be done. This is phase 1 in miniature.

source: Rasmussen (1986) book; Rasmussen, Pejtersen and Goodstein (1994) Cognitive Systems Engineering (as listed on Wikipedia)
finding: Rasmussen's line of work: 1974 paper with Jensen on mental procedures in real tasks, 1983 SRK paper, 1986 book on information processing and human-machine interaction, 1994 CSE book with Pejtersen and Goodstein.
numbers: Dates: 1974, 1983, 1986, 1994, 2000. No data in the page.
limits: Bibliography only; Wikipedia does not explain SRK or the abstraction hierarchy there.
agent_relevance: Primary-source map to cite. Our schema should cite 1983 for the behaviour split and 1986 for the abstraction hierarchy.

source: Wikipedia: Ecological interface design (summary of Vicente and Rasmussen 1990, 1992)
finding: EID makes constraints of the work domain visible. The abstraction hierarchy has five levels: functional purpose, abstract function, generalised function, physical function, physical form. Means-ends links answer how (down) and why (up). SRK gives three behaviour types; supporting skill and rule levels frees capacity for knowledge-based reasoning.
numbers: 5 AH levels; 3 SRK levels. No experimental numbers on the page.
quote: make the work environment's constraints and complex relationships perceptually evident to the user
limits: Page has no DURESS results. Secondary.
agent_relevance: The 5 levels map to a text template an LLM can fill: purpose, laws and constraints, functions, objects, forms. Why/how links give a check on each step.

source: Rasmussen (1983) Skills, rules, knowledge; signals, signs, symbols. IEEE Trans SMC 13:257-266
finding: Splits behaviour into skill-based (automatic sensorimotor), rule-based (stored if-then procedures) and knowledge-based (explicit reasoning from a goal and a model). Error types differ by level.
numbers: No numbers recorded. Not opened; the gist is taken from the Wikipedia EID page (opened) and reference lists of opened papers.
limits: Conceptual framework, not an experiment. McIlroy and Stanton (2015) ask what happened to SRK in practice.
agent_relevance: Gate S0 can use SRK as a router: a familiar pattern goes to a cheap rule path, a novel goal goes to the full schema. Matches G1 (doubt only on a signal).

source: McIlroy and Stanton (2015) Ecological interface design two decades on: whatever happened to the SRK taxonomy? IEEE THMS
finding: Cited as a review asking whether EID designs kept the SRK taxonomy in practice. Only the title was seen, in a reference list.
numbers: Not read; no figures.
limits: Only the citation was opened (Simkute et al. 2024, ref 79).
agent_relevance: Suggests SRK is the weakest-used part of EID; do not build the gate on SRK alone.

source: Simkute et al. (2024) Ironies of Generative AI: productivity loss in human-AI interactions
finding: Perspective paper proposing that GenAI systems follow ecological interface design: show what the user controls and sees together, map domain constraints to interface cues, show key relationships on screen. Says EID reduced workload and raised performance in aviation risk management, medical domains and automation-assisted driving.
numbers: No new measurement of EID. Claims rest on earlier studies (refs 63, 34, 115).
quote: GenAI systems be designed according to an ecological interface design (EID) approach
limits: Perspective paper; the EID benefit is cited, not tested on LLMs.
agent_relevance: EID for LLM tools is a design argument, not a measured gain. Treat as hypothesis.

source: Li and Burns (2017) Modeling automation with cognitive work analysis to support human-automation coordination. JCEDM 11(4):299-322
finding: Adds a degree-of-automation layer on the abstraction hierarchy and decision ladder. Shade the functions the automation handles. In the high-automation trading case, automation takes over higher levels (functional purpose, abstract function), not just physical ones.
numbers: Four modelled cases (low and high automation, routine and unanticipated). 2 hypothetical scenarios. 0 participants, 0 statistics.
limits: Pure modelling. No empirical test. One firm observed. Authors decline to say layering beats the dual-model approach.
agent_relevance: A template for splitting work between program and model: mark which functions the code owns and which the model owns (schema section 1).

source: Li and Burns (2017), citing Rasmussen (1974, 1986), Rasmussen and Goodstein (1987), Mazaeva and Bisantz (2007)
finding: Decision ladder (Rasmussen 1974): activation, observe, identify, interpret, define task, formulate procedure, execute, with shortcuts for experts who skip steps. Rasmussen and Goodstein (1987) used three decision ladders for cooperative decisions in nuclear control. Mazaeva and Bisantz (2007) used a camera abstraction hierarchy plus three decision ladders for a fixed automation level.
numbers: 7 ladder stages; 3 ladders in the 1987 nuclear case.
limits: Secondhand description via a 2017 paper.
agent_relevance: The decision-ladder shortcuts (skip steps when the state is familiar) are the classic basis for a fast path in S0.

source: Li and Burns (2017), citing Onnasch et al. (2014) meta-analysis
finding: The Onnasch et al. meta-analysis is cited as suggesting that ecological displays may modify or reverse the usual automation trade-off in human performance.
numbers: No effect sizes given in the page text.
limits: Only a one-line citation was read; the meta-analysis itself was not opened.
agent_relevance: Candidate source for a real effect size on EID displays; follow up.

source: Telemedicine work domain analysis in a surgical setting (JMIR 2021), using Naikar's method
finding: Used Naikar's abstraction-level prompts to code interviews. Authors say Rasmussen and Vicente give comprehensive but somewhat conflicting descriptions of how to do WDA, while Naikar gives a systematic method. System boundaries were hard to fix, so they modelled facets.
numbers: 20 semistructured interviews: 10 ERCP specialists, 5 assistants, 3 technical staff, 2 administrative; 5 hospitals.
quote: provide comprehensive but somewhat conflicting descriptions of how to conduct WDA
limits: Single case study; no reliability test of the resulting model.
agent_relevance: Boundary setting is a real step: the S0 gate must fix the system boundary before listing constraints.

source: ICU nurse patient-mobility study (JMIR 2022) using Naikar's 9-step WDA method
finding: Built an abstraction hierarchy from documents, observation and interviews, then reviewed it with experts. Steps 6-8 iterate; the last step is validating the hierarchy; means-ends links were added after interviews.
numbers: Observation 32 hours, N=4 nurses; interviews N=20; 2 hospitals; analysis by 2 investigators.
limits: Validation is expert review, not a test of whether the hierarchy predicts anything.
agent_relevance: Models are built by iterate-then-review, like a draft, check, revise loop. Validation stays soft.

source: Modeling patient treatment with medical records: an abstraction hierarchy (2017)
finding: Abstraction hierarchy built from literature and subject-matter experts; AH described as a full depiction of the constraints needed for the system to achieve its purpose. Authors admit no formal grounded-theory method and little clinical validation.
numbers: 8 subject-matter experts, iterated and re-interviewed.
limits: Small expert sample; model called helpful but not perfect.
agent_relevance: Typical evidence level for WDA is expert-reviewed, not quantitatively validated. Do not claim the S0 gate is proven by this literature.

source: Miller, McGuire and Feigh (2017) Decision support requirements for human EVA based on CWA. JCEDM
finding: Used WDA first to find constraints in spacewalk work, then a contextual activity template and decision ladders to turn expert insight into decision-support requirements. Notes CSE requirements are hard to trace and verify later in engineering.
numbers: Of 391 EVAs to July 2016, 110 (28%) had significant incidents. Models validated by follow-up observation and interviews.
limits: Requirements derived, not tested in use here.
agent_relevance: WDA outputs can become a list of testable requirements: a pattern for turning the S0 analysis into checks (G3).

source: Naikar and Elix (2016) Integrated system design: promoting the capacity of sociotechnical systems for adaptation. Front Psychol
finding: Says CWA supports adaptation of behaviour but not of organisational structure. Proposes a work organisation possibilities diagram as an extension. Argues designs should support adaptation to unforeseen events, not scripts for every case.
numbers: Conceptual; no data.
quote: it is not possible to formulate an algorithm, plan, or procedure for every single complication
limits: No empirical test; authors say validation is future research.
agent_relevance: Argument for giving constraints rather than procedures: tell the agent the limits, not the steps. Fits the gate idea but unproven.

source: Burns et al. (2014) Team cognitive work analysis in a birthing unit
finding: Extends CWA with team models derived from teamwork theory. States Vicente's control task analysis asks what needs to be done independent of how or by whom. Notes DURESS operating configurations as an example of strategies analysis.
numbers: Qualitative; no sample statistics extracted.
limits: Single case; supplements, does not replace, CWA.
agent_relevance: The what-versus-how split in control task analysis is the same split as problem class versus method in S0.

source: Wang et al. (2024) Bridging the novice-expert gap via models of decision-making (Bridge)
finding: Cognitive task analysis with 4 expert math teachers gave a 3-step decision model (infer error, pick strategy, state intention). Giving GPT-4 the expert's decisions made responses far more preferred than no decisions. Random decisions hurt. Expert paths were more diverse than LLM paths.
numbers: 700 tutoring conversations; decision-path entropy expert 6.00 vs gpt-4 3.37, gpt-3.5 3.42, llama-2-70b 3.37; +76% preferred and +80% useful for GPT-4; random decisions -97% quality vs expert decisions; p<0.05 on overall score for all models; gpt-3.5 and llama-2 did not gain on care.
limits: Education domain; 4 experts; human preference ratings, not learning outcomes.
agent_relevance: Best direct LLM test of expert task analysis as a scaffold. Context-sensitive decisions matter and random ones hurt, so a wrong gate choice is costly.

source: Figueiredo (2025) Designing smarter conversational agents for kids: lessons from cognitive work and means-ends analyses
finding: Ran CWA with 9 child-parent pairs plus teachers, found three functions (School, Discovery, Entertainment), turned them into structured-prompt conversation recipes, then tested GPT-4o-mini on 1,200 simulated exchanges against an unstructured baseline.
numbers: Study 1: 23 participants over 7 weeks. Study 2: 1,200 exchanges. Similarity to gold: Welch t(2980)=6.16, d=0.225, 95% CI [0.150,0.300]; configuration F(1,2996)=37.90, partial eta2=0.012; question-count IRR=0.004 vanilla vs recipe; question depth rank-biserial 0.167; question diversity IRR 0.26; temperature gave no benefit.
limits: Text proxies only (cosine to gold answer, question counts), no child outcomes; one small model; author-built gold answers.
agent_relevance: CWA-derived modes (a mode gate before answering) change output measurably but modestly (d about 0.2). Cheap to copy: classify mode first, then use a mode recipe.

source: Figueiredo (2025), Study 2 grade-level result
finding: Similarity to the gold answer varied by grade: grade 1 higher than grades 9 and 12 (p<.001).
limits: Tiny effect (eta2 about 1.5%).
agent_relevance: The gate's value varies by problem type. Measure it per class.

source: Kopka and Feufel (2026) Increasing LLM accuracy for care-seeking advice using prompts reflecting human reasoning (JMIR Biomed Eng)
finding: Tested 10 ChatGPT models with default, recognition-primed and data-frame prompts on 45 patient vignettes. Prompts built from human reasoning theory raised accuracy a little, mostly for self-care. Authors name the decision ladder as another model one could use but did not test it.
numbers: Accuracy: default 63.3%, recognition-primed 67.6%, data-frame 66.7%. Self-care: 13.4% default vs 29.8% and 24.6%. 10 runs per model-vignette-prompt; 3 urgency levels; the 2 emergency and 30 nonemergency cases stayed high.
limits: Only 45 vignettes, one vendor family; the NDM overlap belongs to another subfield (Naturalistic decision making).
agent_relevance: Theory-shaped prompts give about 3-4 points here. The decision ladder remains an untested prompt scaffold for LLMs.

source: ACTIVE problem solving (2026) uses Rasmussen's abstraction hierarchy for complex problems
finding: Method for complex or chaotic problems that uses work domain analysis, bottom-up from physical form to functional purpose, to separate essential function from incidental physical detail, paired with morphological analysis.
numbers: No effect sizes extracted; method paper.
limits: Not tested against a baseline; I did not verify any LLM use.
agent_relevance: Shows the abstraction hierarchy reused as a general problem-framing tool outside engineering: restate a task by function, not by surface form.

source: Mussi et al. (2025) Human-AI interaction in safety-critical network infrastructures (iScience)
finding: Perspective on power, rail and air traffic. Says EID shows constraints, relations and action opportunities at all abstraction levels, and joint cognitive framework decides when to show which level. Cites Borst et al. on EID concerns and misconceptions.
numbers: No experiments.
limits: Perspective article.
agent_relevance: Constraints shown at several abstraction levels only when the situation demands. Echoes widening the frame only on a signal.

source: Designing for confidence (2022): EID used to interpret explainable-AI visualisation results
finding: Two studies of AI decision visualisations; EID, cognitive fit and situation awareness used to interpret results. Cognitive load did not mediate the confidence-trust link.
numbers: Study 1 N=206 (of 350 recruited); Study 2 N=19 with eye tracking; mediation via load not significant (p=0.47 and p=0.969).
limits: EID is an interpretation lens here, not the tested manipulation.
agent_relevance: EID language is often applied after the fact. Do not count this as a test of EID.

source: Morice et al. (2021) Ecological design of augmentation improves helicopter ship landing (PLoS ONE)
finding: A display built on the perceptual variable the pilot already uses (tau-dot kept near -0.5) shortened landing duration and improved control, compared with an occlusion-fix augmentation. Novices in a VR simulator.
numbers: Ideal tau-dot -0.5; effect sizes not extracted in this session.
limits: Gibsonian ecological design, narrower than Rasmussen's work-domain EID; novices only.
agent_relevance: Matching the display to the real constraint beat generic help; weak link to LLM work.

source: Pawlak and Vicente (1996) Inducing effective operator control through ecological interface design. Int J Human-Computer Studies 44
finding: Core DURESS-era experiment: an interface showing abstraction-hierarchy constraints was reported to help operators control a process more effectively. Details not retrieved.
numbers: No numbers recorded. Not opened. Needs exact N, conditions and effect sizes from the paper.
limits: Paywalled; tooling blocked. Do not quote specifics from here.
agent_relevance: Key experiment to pull next. Until read, the EID benefit stays unquantified in our notes.

source: Christoffersen, Hunter and Vicente (1996, 1997) DURESS II studies of fault diagnosis with an ecological interface
finding: Series reported better diagnosis of faults, especially novel ones, with the ecological interface than with a conventional one. Details not retrieved.
numbers: No numbers recorded. Not opened.
limits: From memory of the literature; the DOI needs checking. Participants were students on a simulated feedwater system, so transfer to experts is open.
agent_relevance: Novel-fault diagnosis is the closest human analogue to our out-of-class problems.

source: Vicente (1999) as cited across the opened applications papers
finding: Across opened papers Vicente (1999) is cited for: complex sociotechnical systems with high variability, adaptation as a design goal, control task analysis as what, independent of how or by whom, and WDA as a base template.
numbers: No numbers.
limits: Secondhand.
agent_relevance: Convergent citation pattern; these definitions are safe to use in the schema.

source: Gap check: arXiv search for LLM tests of work domain analysis
finding: arXiv full-text searches this session for work domain analysis, abstraction hierarchy plus Rasmussen, means-ends plus work domain, and ecological interface returned 0 to 1 hits. Nothing found tests an abstraction-hierarchy prompt on an LLM.
numbers: work domain analysis = 0 results; abstraction hierarchy + Rasmussen = 0; means-ends + work domain = 0; ecological interface = 1 (Simkute 2024).
limits: Search coverage limited to arXiv; other APIs were rate limited.
agent_relevance: A WDA-based S0 gate would be a new test, not a copy. Plan a small A/B in our harness.

source: Jalaeian, Morey and Rayo (2025) Joint activity design heuristics for human-machine collaboration
finding: Synthesises 14 design heuristics from cognitive systems engineering, aimed at five macrocognitive functions: event detection, sensemaking, adaptability, perspective-shifting, coordination. Does not use work domain analysis.
numbers: 14 heuristics; 5 functions; no experiment seen in the text I read.
limits: Link only; the abstraction hierarchy does not appear.
agent_relevance: Adjacent subfield (coordination and common ground); note the link only.
